expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: No — and specifically, that check cannot fire in the case that caused this incident... Rung: Warning at best, and one that stays silent in the failure mode it was written for.

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: Check-then-act race (M5). Two consumers pass the check concurrently, both charge.

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: Required idempotency key in the signature — not Optional, no default.

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: Unique constraint on (charge_scope, idempotency_key), reserved in the same transaction as recording the charge.

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Defect: 340 customers charged twice. Mistake: the redelivered message ran the charge path a second time. Hazard: charge() carries no identity...

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: the charge call has no idempotency key, and nothing requires one — framed as a system design property, not worker error

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: search for every at-least-once consumer with an external effect: refunds (including the 340 you just issued — was that job retry-safe?), payout creation, subscription create/cancel, transactional email, webhook fan-out, inventory decrement.

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: The second time is its own finding... If it was also an application-level check, the pattern isn't payments — it's that your retros terminate at informative inspection instead of at a constraint. That's the thing to fix once.

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: Worker timed out → queue redelivered (correct — at-least-once is the contract, not the bug)... the charge call has no idempotency key
